subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should distinct ACP child sessions remain parallel by default while fixing launch readiness, or should OpenClaw add a deliberate concurrency gate for ACPX/Claude spawns?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs preserve distinct-session parallelism, so changing that behavior is a product/compatibility choice unless live proof identifies a narrower launch-readiness defect.

options.title: Preserve parallelism and fix readiness
options.body: Recommended: reproduce the two-spawn failure live, then repair ACPX/OpenClaw startup readiness or error reporting without serializing all distinct ACP sessions.

options.title: Add an explicit ACPX concurrency gate
options.body: Introduce a documented, tested throttle only if maintainers decide ACPX/Claude cannot safely handle distinct-session launches in parallel.

options.title: Wait for stronger reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue open as needs-info until a maintainer or reporter provides current logs that identify whether the first child was never launched, crashed, or blocked.

recommendation.title: Preserve parallelism and fix readiness
recommendation.body: Recommended: reproduce the two-spawn failure live, then repair ACPX/OpenClaw startup readiness or error reporting without serializing all distinct ACP sessions.
